questions.q: What does the standard error of the mean measure?
options: How spread out individual observations are around the sample mean
How far the sample mean would typically vary across repeated samples
How biased the sampling method is
The difference between the largest and smallest values
questions.explain: Standard error is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of a statistic; it describes the precision of the estimate, not the spread of individual values.

questions.q: A sample of 50 orders has sd 26.67. What is the standard error of the mean?
options: About 3.77
About 26.67
About 0.53
About 1,333
questions.explain: SE = s / sqrt(n) = 26.67 / 7.07, which is about 3.77.

questions.q: You increase the sample size from 100 to 400 (same population). What is the expected effect on the standard error?
options: It stays the same
It doubles
It falls to about a quarter
It falls to about half
questions.explain: SE is proportional to 1/sqrt(n). Going from n = 100 to n = 400 multiplies n by 4 and so divides the SE by 2.

questions.q: Why do numpy users write sample.std(ddof=1) when estimating a population's spread from a sample?
options: It divides by n - 1, giving an unbiased estimate of the population variance
It makes the result run faster
It converts the result to a standard error
It removes outliers
questions.explain: numpy's default divides by n (ddof=0), which slightly underestimates spread in a sample. ddof=1 divides by n - 1.

questions.q: A survey has a very small standard error but only surveyed customers who opened a promotional email. What is the most accurate conclusion?
options: The estimate is precise and therefore accurate
The small SE proves there is no bias
The standard error must have been computed incorrectly
The estimate may be precise but still biased, since SE ignores how the sample was collected
questions.explain: SE captures only random sampling error. Selection bias can shift the estimate no matter how small the SE is.
